system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar turbulence: conflicts, contagion and market shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system under strain as regional wars, domestic political crises and great-power maneuvering interact with volatile energy and capital markets. Middle East escalation and Russian strategic moves amplify supply and security shocks while Western democratic instability and US policy swings weaken alliance coherence. Economic friction — from China’s trade and tech controls to emerging-market stress — transmits rapidly through financial markets and commodity prices, creating feedbacks that reshape diplomatic space and domestic politics.
system_description.scope: State and non-state actors, regional conflicts, alliance politics, sanctions and trade measures, global energy and commodity flows, international finance and capital markets, major technology and information platforms, migration and humanitarian systems — and the institutional responses that connect them.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio‑economic‑political system (the Anthropocene-era global civilization in which geopolitics, markets, ecology and technology interact).
adjacent_subsystems: Regional security complexes (Middle East, Europe, Indo‑Pacific, Africa)

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war dynamics
variables.description: Ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, with Western backers, in which battlefield tactics, strikes on energy and infrastructure and shifting diplomacy are altering the war’s trajectory and support calculus.

variables.name: Middle East maritime and energy flashpoint
variables.description: Escalating attacks by Iran-aligned proxies (notably the Houthis) and Iranian maritime actions against Saudi and regional targets, drawing in Saudi-led and Western forces, are disrupting shipping security and threatening hydrocarbon export routes.

variables.name: US–China tech and trade rivalry
variables.description: A deepening strategic competition between the United States and China over export controls, semiconductors, AI technologies, rare-earths and industrial policy is fragmenting supply chains and technological interdependence.

variables.name: Western political fragmentation and unrest
variables.description: Rising domestic polarization, mass protests and populist gains across Western democracies — from violent French unrest to US electoral turbulence — are weakening governance, shifting political balances and stressing allied cohesion.

variables.name: Global market and capital-flow fragility
variables.description: Financial-system stress spanning advanced and emerging markets — driven by higher interest rates, bond-yield shocks, index reclassifications (MSCI), housing weakness and political shocks — is amplifying volatility and cross-border contagion risks.
